I reviewed `artifacts/editorial/release-candidates/housing/burnaby-tenant-protection-bylaw-now-in-effect.mdx` against the pipeline's research, scorecard, and learning artifacts, plus the published image assets. I found no correction needed before publication. Note on scope: this session has no shell or web access, so I could not independently recompute the hash or fetch the live burnaby.ca pages; the verdict rests on the file at the stated canonical path and on internal/repo evidence.

**Factual support and source use.** Every substantive claim is explicitly attributed ("The City of Burnaby says…", "The bylaw document says…") to one of four primary City of Burnaby sources, all listed in both the Sources section and the research record at `artifacts/editorial/research/2026-07-19-midday-food-housing-candidates.json:70-91` (evidenceStrength 5, score 91, verdict release-candidate). Internal dates are mutually consistent: Council approval May 26, announcement URL dated May 28, effective July 1, previous policy 2015 to June 30. The one genuine ambiguity — whether a June 30 application falls under the old or new stream — is handled transparently by telling readers to confirm with the city rather than asserting an answer, which is the right treatment.

**Title/meta fit.** Title, subtitle, and description accurately describe the content with no overreach; the description matches the article's actual coverage (who is covered, supports, what to check first).

**Structure and reader usefulness.** Clear progression (what changed → who is covered → what supports → checklist), concrete decision points keyed to application dates, and named contact points (Burnaby Renters Office, Tenant Relocation Coordinator). This is a genuinely useful renter explainer, consistent with the storyType `guide-or-explainer`.

**Image and frontmatter integrity.** The image exists at both `public/images/editorial/2026/07/burnaby-tenant-protection-bylaw.png` and the `apps/web/public` mirror (the earlier path issue was fixed in commit 259db4b). I viewed the image: moving boxes, keys, apartment buildings with construction cranes — it matches the alt text, shows no identifiable face, and the attribution correctly discloses it as AI-generated editorial art. Slug matches the filename, category matches the directory, timestamps are plausible for the run, and readingTime of 4 is reasonable for ~620 words.

**Reputational/legal risk.** Low. The piece includes an explicit "not legal advice" disclaimer, defers to official city and Residential Tenancy Branch processes, names no individuals or private businesses, and makes no claims beyond what it attributes to the city. The learning record confirms no sensitive-approval gate was triggered.

Minor non-blocking observation: the phrase "applications submitted before June 30" alongside "policy ran to June 30" is slightly awkward, but the article already flags the boundary case explicitly, so no change is required.
